# 🛡️ Welcome to the nftban Community!

nftban is a modern, modular Linux firewall framework built around nftables, Fail2Ban, and intelligent automation. We use GitHub Discussions as our main place to connect, share, and collaborate with sysadmins, security engineers, and testers.

---

## 💬 What You Can Do Here

- **Ask questions** about installation, configuration, and tuning on Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, Rocky, Alma, or Fedora
- **Share ideas** or feature proposals that improve security, automation, or usability
- **Post results** from beta testing, performance benchmarking, or module experiments
- **Engage with others** — exchange best practices and security insights
- **Help improve nftban** by discussing architecture or suggesting code optimizations

---

## 🧩 Community Principles

We keep things:

- **Professional and open** — respect Linux diversity and deployment environments
- **Transparent** — credit both human and AI contributions
- **Collaborative** — every tester and partner strengthens nftban's protection layer

---

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Introduce Yourself!

Tell us:
- Your Linux environment (e.g., Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, RHEL 9)
- How you deploy nftban (CLI, automation, containers, etc.)
- Which modules you're exploring (DDoS, GeoIP, Feeds, Fail2Ban...)
- Any ideas you'd like to test or refine

💡 **Tip for new contributors**: Discussions are ideal for brainstorming and testing feedback. Confirmed bugs should still go to [Issues](https://github.com/itcmsgr/nftban/issues).

---

## 📌 Discussion Categories

### 💡 Ideas & Feature Requests
Propose enhancements, new modules, or workflow improvements.

### 🧪 Beta Testing & Feedback
Share v0.9.0 beta results, migration experiences, and observations.

### 🙋 Q&A
Ask installation, configuration, and troubleshooting questions.

### 📢 Announcements
Project updates, releases, and important changes (maintained by project team).

### 🗣️ General
Everything else — show & tell, use cases, integrations, and community chat.

## 💬 Community Guidelines

- **Be respectful** — treat all members professionally
- **Search first** — check if your question has been answered
- **Provide details** — include OS, version, commands, and outputs when asking questions
- **Stay on topic** — use appropriate categories
- **Give back** — help others when you can
